The instruction told WebSurfer to find 'sample standard deviations' directly on ScienceDirect, whereas the task requires retrieving the underlying counts of Reference Works by subdomains (for Life Sciences and for Health Sciences) in 2022 and then computing the sample standard deviations. Step 1 correctly aimed to gather counts; step 2 shifted the goal to searching for precomputed standard deviations, which likely do not exist on ScienceDirect and led the process astray.

Yes. They did not pivot to gathering per-domain counts of Reference Works from ScienceDirect and computing the sample SDs themselves. No step explicitly attempts to list counts by Life Sciences and Health Sciences sub-domains and pass them to Coder for calculation, so the initial mistake was not corrected.
